div.p: [From the South Pacific Times, Tuesday, November 19, 1878.]

Don Manuel Pardo, Ex-President of the republic, leader of the political party now predominant in the country, senator for the department of Junin, and president of the Senate, has been the victim of a perfidious and cowardly assassination, committed within the very sanctuary of the law, by one of those placed there to protect it. The foul hand of the assassin, the blackest treason, the most horrible crime, has rudely ended an illustrious existence.

The president of the Senate, while on his way to assume the duties of his august position, and whilst the honors due to the elevated rank conferred on him by the law and the will of the people were being paid him, was, almost at the same moment, struck down by the mortiferous projectile which issued from an arm placed by the nation in the hands of one of its servants for the purpose of defending its honor. This is strange and unprecedented in a country where the kindness and mildness of its inhabitants are as remarkable as is their repugnance for everything infamous and criminal.

The entire nation, without distinction of party or of political creed, and with it every honorable man, be his nationality what it may, bitterly deplores this terrible calamity, unique of its kind, which it considers as a stain never to be effaced, and whose authors merit universal execration.

Who are the miserable wretches that have thus wounded their mother-country to its heart’s core? So infamous a crime has undoubtedly been instigated in the darkness by treason, cowardice, and envy, the implacable enemies of all that is good. It cannot have been the result of political fanaticism, for this produces heroes, not vile and miserable assassins who treacherously wound and then seek safety in cowardly flight; much less can it he attributed to personal vengeance, as some have conjectured, for this could have been realized in another manner and under other and less aggravating circumstances. A deed of this nature can have no other origin than a horrible intrigue, participated in by depraved wretches who dishonor the society of which they are members.

The investigations now being actively made, and the declaration of the assassin himself, who was fortunately apprehended, lead to the suspicion that such a presumption is not devoid of foundation. Should it be confirmed, we are convinced that the weight of the law will fall upon the delinquents with all the rigor demanded by public vengeance and in the interest of society.

The members of the foreign communities established in the country, who, with the strictest impartiality, have been able to appreciate the noble qualities of the distinguished statesman, the valiant patriot, the good citizen, and the exemplary parent, and who measure with sound, judgment the enormity of the crime of which he has been the victim, unite themselves to the sons of the soil in the manifestation of the profound sorrow by which they are moved for the irreparable loss experienced by the nation.

The mourning is general, just, and spontaneous, and in thus expressing it, clothing to-day the columns of the South Pacific Times in their mourning garb, we make ourselves the interpreters of the public sentiment, which we most sincerely share.
We also fulfill a solemn duty in conveying to the desolate family of the illustrious victim and to the entire nation our heartfelt expressions of sympathy.
The following proclamation was published on Saturday afternoon by the President of the Republic:
“The President of the Republic to the Nation:

“Fellow-Citizens: An atrocious crime, unique of its kind in the annals of Peru, has been committed to-day, in broad daylight, and the august threshold of the Senate, in the person of his excellency the president of that honorable chamber, Don Manuel Pardo, A wretched soldier, who can only be the blind tool of a premeditated crime, has been the perpetrator of this horrible assassination, which has deeply affected the government, and which will meet with the condemnation of the whole country.
“Immediately upon receiving the fatal news, I hurried to the theater of the crime, but all efforts were useless to save the illustrious victim, who expired a few moments later.

“The criminal was instantly apprehended, and justice has already set on foot his trial, which will be actively carried on, and whose results will satisfy the public craving for due punishment of the assassin, and will likewise serve as a salutary warning against the repetition of such crime.
“Fellow-citizens, you cannot but unite with the government in condemning and punishing such a monstrous crime, one of fatal remembrance for the country.
